data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"As n grows, the probability of reaching unanimous consensus tends to 0; it is exp(-\u0398(n)). The finite obstruction structures are locally stable mixed configurations in which every vertex agrees with the majority of its three neighbors and the bichromatic edges form a matching cut; in particular, perfect-matching complements that are 2-factors colored monochromatically on each cycle are stable mixed states.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the random 3-regular graph is conditioned to be an expander with no large matching cuts, the exp(-\u0398(n)) law fails and consensus probability may tend to 1.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the initial coloring is not uniformly random but biased toward one color, the consensus probability may be 1 - o(1).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Each update of a vertex with two or three opposite neighbors strictly decreases the number of bichromatic edges, so the process is a monotone descent to an absorbing state. Consensus is the zero-bichromatic-edge absorbing state. Stable mixed states are exactly matching cuts: every vertex has at most one opposite neighbor, so no vertex flips. A random 3-regular graph has exponentially many perfect matchings; removing one leaves a 2-factor, and coloring each cycle monochromatically gives a stable mixed configuration. The expected number of such obstruction structures is exp(\u0398(n)), and their basins cover all but an exp(-\u0398(n)) fraction of initial colorings, so the probability of consensus is exp(-\u0398(n)).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
